text: The following question stood in the name of  Miss Cheng Li Hui –  4  To ask the Minister for Health (a) how long have public hospitals been engaging foreign agents to bring in overseas patients; (b) whether the Ministry is aware of these practices; and (c) whether the foreign patients crowd out Singaporeans in our healthcare services.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: asked the Minister for Health whether the Ministry will reschedule or bring forward the specialist appointment dates of subsidised Singaporean patients arising from the Ministry's decision to stop referral contracts for foreign patients in public hospitals.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: There are foreign patients who travel to Singapore to seek medical treatment on their own accord.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Those whose referrals were supported by contracted service providers constituted about only 0.4% of attendances in PHIs that had such contracts.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Singaporeans remained the majority of patients treated in the PHIs.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Foreign patients have not impacted our PHI's delivery of services and subsidised appointment slots given to Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: MOH will continue to work with our PHIs to ensure that meeting Singaporean's healthcare needs remains our priority.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: My Parliamentary Question was actually prompted by a resident who saw me in late August.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: He had been referred by a polyclinic for a specialist appointment for a colonoscopy procedure.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: These were the resident's words and I narrated this to the Singapore General Hospital (SGH).

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: One of the hospital's staff told him that only one day of the week is set aside for subsidised patients for colonoscopy procedures and that is the reason why his appointment was scheduled six months later.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: SGH came back a couple of weeks later.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: They contacted the resident and they pushed forward the appointment by three months, and so, he only had to wait three months.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: So, that is reason why I actually asked the question whether, firstly, there is any truth to this assumption or allegation that there are specific days set aside for non-subsidised patients and other days for subsidised patients, be it for inpatient procedures or other procedures not limited to colonoscopies.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The second question I have is pertaining to a reply that the Senior Minister of State gave that between the years 2013 and 2017, 1.5% of foreigners were registered for inpatient or day surgeries in our public hospitals.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: But what is the number, the absolute number of that, as opposed to a percentage?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I believe earlier in October, there was an MOH reply to The Sunday Times clarifying that this number is actually lower than what it was in 2008.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: At that time, it was 2.4% if I remember correctly.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Just to get a sense of the absolute numbers, I would appreciate if the Senior Minister of State could share the total number of foreign patients, vis-a-vis both percentages.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: On the first clarification, many hospitals do have a protocol to prioritise the appointment given to patients according to the severity of the conditions.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: If the condition is deemed to be urgent, then the appointment given will be much shorter or almost immediate.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And if the condition is assessed to be not urgent, then the appointment date given can be much further away.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: It could be a few weeks or a few months, depending on the type of condition.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As to the feedback given by one of his residents, I would find it hard to believe that only one day in a week will be assigned for colonoscopy for subsidised patients, considering the fact that the department in SGH is actually a large one with multiple specialists performing such procedures.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But I think that needs to be clarified with SGH.
